bleeding (minor): Wash your hands if possible and put on disposable gloves if available.
Apply direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth for several minutes.
Clean gently with water and apply an adhesive bandage.
Seek medical help if bleeding continues or the wound is deep.
severe bleeding: Apply firm direct pressure to the wound using a clean cloth or dressing.
If possible, elevate the injured area above heart level unless a fracture is suspected.
Do not remove soaked dressings; add more layers and maintain pressure.
choking (adult or child): If the person can cough or speak, encourage them to cough to expel the object.
If they cannot breathe, perform abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) for adults and older children.
For infants under 1 year, give five back blows followed by five chest thrusts.
If the person becomes unconscious, call emergency services and begin CPR.
heart attack: Have the person sit down and try to keep them calm; loosen tight clothing.
If available and not allergic, give one adult aspirin to chew slowly.
Monitor breathing and be prepared to perform CPR if they lose consciousness.
stroke: Call emergency services immediately and note the time symptoms began.
Ask the person to smile, raise both arms, and repeat a simple sentence to check for weakness or slurred speech.
Keep the person comfortable and lying down with head slightly elevated.
Do not give food, drink, or medication unless instructed by professionals.
burn (minor): Remove the person from the source of the burn and stop the burning process.
Cool the burn under running cool (not cold) water for 10–20 minutes.
Do not apply ice, butter, or creams; cover loosely with a sterile non-stick dressing.
Seek medical help if the burn is large or causes severe pain.
fracture (suspected): Do not move the injured limb unnecessarily; support and immobilize with a splint if available.
Apply ice packs wrapped in cloth to reduce swelling (avoid direct contact with skin).
If bone is protruding, cover with sterile dressing and seek immediate medical attention.
Treat for shock and keep the person comfortable until help arrives.
snake bite: Keep the person calm and still; immobilize the bitten limb and keep it lower than the heart.
Remove rings, watches or tight clothing from the bitten area due to swelling.
Do not cut the wound, use a tourniquet, or try to suck out venom.
Get the person to hospital as quickly as possible.
poisoning (ingestion): Call your local poison control center or emergency services immediately.
If the person is unconscious or having seizures, call emergency services right away.
Do not induce vomiting unless instructed by medical professionals.
If the container is available, take it with you to the hospital for identification.
drowning (near-drowning): Get the person out of the water safely as soon as possible.
If not breathing, start CPR immediately and call emergency services.
If breathing, place in the recovery position and monitor closely.
Seek medical evaluation even if the person seems to recover.
fall from height: Call emergency services immediately if the fall is significant or the person is injured.
Do not move the person if you suspect spinal or head injury unless there's immediate danger.
Check breathing and circulation; begin CPR if necessary.
Keep the person warm and monitor for signs of shock until help arrives.
slipped on steps / fall on stairs: Help the person lie down and assess for pain or bleeding.
If they complain of severe neck, back, or head pain, do not move them and call emergency services.
For minor injuries, apply ice to reduce swelling and keep the injured area elevated.
If there is loss of consciousness, confusion, severe pain, or vomiting, seek immediate medical attention.
concussion / head injury: Call emergency services if the person is unconscious, vomiting, has seizures, or shows confusion.
Keep the person still and lying with head raised slightly unless spinal injury is suspected.
Monitor pupils, breathing, and responsiveness; wake them periodically if advised by professionals.
Seek medical assessment for any suspected head injury, even if symptoms seem mild.
road traffic accident / major trauma: Call emergency services immediately and provide the location and nature of injuries.
Do not move seriously injured persons unless there is an immediate life threat.
Control bleeding with direct pressure and treat for shock (cover with blanket, keep warm).
Provide simple reassurance and monitor airway, breathing, and circulation until help arrives.
